text_blocks.snippet: Core inflation is a measure of inflation that excludes volatile components like food and energy prices. It aims to provide a clearer, more stable picture of underlying price trends, helping policymakers assess the true state of inflation and make informed decisions about interest rates.
snippet_highlighted_words: a measure of inflation that excludes volatile components like food and energy prices

list.title: Headline Inflation vs. Core Inflation:
list.snippet: "Headline inflation" includes all items in the consumer price index (CPI), encompassing everything from food and energy to clothing and housing. Core inflation, on the other hand, strips out food and energy prices, which tend to fluctuate significantly due to various factors like weather, seasonal changes, and global events.
